issues: The oversized black band beneath the helmet merges with the face and body, creating a heavy void unlike the compact, clearly separated forms of MM2/MM3 enemies.
The two white eye clusters are blocky and uneven; at 1x they can read as teeth rather than eyes.
The lower body lacks a clear round contour and is mostly undefined black space.
The left foot/leg forms a long diagonal orange staircase, while the right foot is a disconnected rectangular block, making the walking anatomy inconsistent.
The helmet highlight is large and angular, competing with the face instead of acting as a restrained one-pixel accent.
Several silhouette transitions, especially the helmet's lower corners and left leg, are jagged rather than deliberately stepped.
fixes: Reduce the helmet brim to a consistent one-pixel black edge and expose another row of the face beneath it.
Redraw each eye as a compact matching white cluster with a clear black pupil or separation, keeping both on the same baseline.
Add a small rounded body contour under the eyes using two- to three-pixel orange clusters instead of leaving one large black cavity.
Rebuild both feet as similarly sized two- or three-pixel-wide forms, separated from the body by one black pixel.
Shorten the left diagonal appendage and remove its staircase tail so it reads as a stubby walking foot.
Shrink the helmet highlight to a compact one-pixel-thick patch and simplify the shell into cleaner Capcom-style stepped curves.

issues: The two white shapes beneath the helmet brim read more like teeth than eyes; they lack clear pupils and eye framing at 1x.
The exposed black body is angular and hollow-looking rather than a small round robot body.
The lower-left orange appendage has an unclear silhouette, reading as a bent tail or loose cluster rather than a foot or cannon.
The helmet's central black plus-shaped detail is visually busy and not a typical Mega Man construction-helmet accent.
Using black, orange, pale peach, and white creates a four-color sprite treatment; the separate white and peach highlights feel less disciplined than typical MM2/MM3 enemy palettes.
The feet are unevenly designed: the right foot is a large highlighted wedge while the left side merges into the ambiguous appendage.
fixes: Redraw each eye as a compact white 2x2 or 3x2 cluster with a clearly placed 1-pixel black pupil, separated by one black pixel.
Round the body silhouette by adding one pixel at each lower side and removing angular black notches around the torso.
Replace the lower-left zigzag with a simple 3-4-pixel-wide stubby foot, or shape it into a clearly horizontal cannon muzzle with a black opening.
Remove the helmet's plus-shaped mark or reduce it to a simple 1-2-pixel seam or highlight cluster.
Use black, orange, and one light color consistently; make both the eyes and highlights share a legal three-color-per-sprite solution or use an intentional overlay.
Make both feet similarly sized, with compact orange clusters and one consistent light-color highlight on their upper edges.

issues: The three large white blocks beneath the brim read more like teeth than two eyes.
The black cross and large white patch on the helmet create busy, nonstandard surface detail for a Mega Man 2-3 enemy.
The long diagonal orange cluster at lower left makes the leg silhouette look like a tail or bent tube rather than a stubby foot.
The right-side orange vertical cluster is ambiguous and does not clearly read as a limb, body edge, or weapon.
Several contour steps around the lower body and feet are chunky and irregular compared with Capcom's tightly controlled 1-pixel stair-stepping.
The helmet reads immediately, but the body anatomy and shooting role are unclear at 1x.
fixes: Replace the white face pattern with exactly two compact 2x2 or 2x3 eye clusters, separated by at least one black pixel.
Remove the black helmet cross and reduce the white highlight to one small, coherent 2-4 pixel cluster near the upper-left curve.
Shorten the lower-left appendage and place two compact feet directly beneath the body with matching one-pixel black soles.
Either remove the isolated orange cluster on the right or reshape it into a clearly outlined two- or three-pixel muzzle.
Redraw the lower silhouette using cleaner one-pixel staircase transitions and eliminate the thin diagonal connection into the left foot.
Keep the strong orange, white, black, and transparent palette; the existing color discipline is appropriately NES-like.

issues: The sprite appears roughly 23x22 px, making it broader and heavier than the intended compact 20x19 enemy.
The black cross-shaped cluster near the helmet's left-center looks accidental rather than like Capcom-style construction or shading.
The white clusters beneath the brim resemble three teeth or a zigzag mouth instead of two clearly separated eyes on a round body.
The large black cavity under the helmet obscures the body's shape, especially at 1x.
The long diagonal orange connection to the left foot is awkward and makes the walking pose look bent or partially melted.
The right foot's pale inset adds detail where a simpler, stronger cluster would read better.
fixes: Compress the design by two or three pixels in width and height while retaining the helmet-heavy silhouette.
Replace the black cross in the helmet with a compact 2x2 or 2x3 light highlight and uninterrupted orange around it.
Redraw the face as exactly two separated 2x2 light eye clusters inside a small rounded black body.
Reduce the empty black area beneath the brim and define the body's lower curve with a clean one-pixel contour.
Shorten the left leg to a one- or two-pixel joint and build each foot as a compact 3-4 pixel orange cluster.
Remove the pale foot inset and reserve the light color for the eyes and one helmet highlight.
Keep each contour stair-step deliberate, especially along the brim ends and lower feet, to match MM2/MM3 cluster economy.

issues: The black cross-shaped cut and long horizontal black stripe inside the helmet crown read as arbitrary gouges rather than Capcom-style shading or construction detail.
Under the brim, the repeated white notched clusters resemble teeth; two distinct eyes and a small round body are not immediately clear at 1x.
The torso collapses into a large black void, weakening the separation between face, body, and legs.
The lower-left leg has a long, uneven diagonal staircase, while the right foot is a bulky orange block; the walking pose feels unbalanced.
The pale-orange helmet highlight is large and angular without clearly describing the dome.
Using black, orange, pale orange, and white within the same small regions risks exceeding normal NES sprite-palette discipline unless built from deliberate overlays.
fixes: Remove the crown's black cross and horizontal gouge; describe the helmet with one uninterrupted orange mass, a clean black contour, and a compact 1-2-pixel pale-orange highlight.
Redraw the face as two clearly separated white eye blocks with single black pupils, leaving black spacing around them so they cannot read as teeth.
Expose a small rounded body beneath the eyes using orange or a contrasting NES color instead of leaving the entire torso black.
Shorten and regularize the left leg's diagonal into clean 1-pixel steps; make both feet compact, similarly weighted clusters while retaining a walking offset.
Simplify the brim into a consistent one-pixel black edge with a clean orange band and avoid isolated protruding pixels at its ends.
Keep each 8x8 region to black plus two opaque colors where possible, or make any extra eye color an intentional sprite-overlay layer.
